grades.quote: If the implementation does not provide ASIDs, or software chooses to always use ASID 0, then after every_ `satp` _write, software should execute SFENCE.VMA with rs1=_ `x0` _.
grades.reason: Directly explains when SFENCE.VMA is required after satp changes (ASID recycling, no ASIDs or ASID 0 after every satp write) and how to set rs1/rs2. It also notes that satp.MODE and ASID changes take effect immediately without a fence.
Covers mtimecmp and the time CSR shadow. It has nothing to do with satp or translation synchronization.
This is a version 1.10 changelog. It only says SFENCE.VM was replaced by SFENCE.VMA and gives no guidance on synchronization after a satp write.

grades.quote: If a hart employs an address-translation cache, that cache must appear to be private to that hart. In particular, the meaning of an ASID is local to a hart
grades.reason: Gives auxiliary context on SFENCE.VMA and address-translation caches. The cache is private to each hart and ASIDs are hart-local. It also notes SFENCE.VMA may trap if satp.MODE is read-only Bare. It does not say when to execute the fence after a satp change.
